FOUNDATION LAYOUT NOTES:
CONCRETE:
1. ALL CONCRETE SHALL BE TxDOT CLASS C (3600 PSI @ 28 DAYS). NO ADDITIVES SHALL BE USED WITHOUT
THE PRIOR APPROVAL OF THE ENGINEER.
2. MAXIMUM AGGREGATE SIZE SHALL NOT EXCEED 1.5".
3. ALL PIER HOLES SHALL BE DRY AND CLEAN PRIOR TO PLACING CONCRETE. PIER HOLES SHALL ONLY BE
DRILLED WITHIN 24 HOURS OF PLACING CONCRETE. CASING SHALL BE REQUIRED WHEN NECESSARY TO
PREVENT CAVING OF THE SOIL AND TO SEAL SURFACE WATER.
4. COLD WEATHER PROCEDURE SHALL APPLY BELOW 40 DEGREES F, PER A.C.I. 306.
5. NO CONCRETE HOTTER THAN 95 DEGREES F. SHALL BE PLACED.
6. DURING HOT WEATHER, CONCRETE SHALL BE KEPT MOIST FOR AT LEAST ONE DAY OR TREATED WITH
MEMBRANE TYPE CURING COMPOUND TO MINIMIZE SURFACE CRACKING. ADDITIONAL HOT WEATHER
PROCEDURES SHALL APPLY DURING HOT WEATHER CONCRETING PER A.C.I. 305R.
7. CHAMFER ALL EXPOSED EDGES 3/4" UNLESS NOTED OTHERWISE.
8. LEVELING NUTS SHALL BE USED ON ALL STRUCTURES SUPPORTED BY PIERS AND SECURED IN PLACE BY
ANCHOR BOLTS. DISTANCE BETWEEN THE TOP OF CONCRETE AND THE BOTTOM OF BASE PLATE SHALL
BE EQUAL TO OR LESS THAN TWO TIMES THE DIAMETER OF THE ANCHOR BOLT.
9. ALL FOUNDATION DESIGNS ARE PERFORMED IN ACCORDANCE WITH A.C.I. STANDARD 318-08.
10. SQUARE CAP DEPTH SHALL BE BELOW SUBGRADE ELEVATION AS SHOWN ON FOUNDATION DETAILS.
11. MONOLITHIC CONCRETE APPLICATIONS ARE DESIRED. BUT, IF MORE THAN ONE POUR IS NECESSARY THE
FOLLOWING PROCEDURE SHALL BE IMPLEMENTED:
A. CONCRETE IN INITIAL POUR TO BE LEFT PILED HIGH IN CENTER OF PIER.
B. AFTER FIRST HOUR, PIER HOLES SHALL BE COVERED WITH PLASTIC UNTIL READY FOR SECOND POUR.
C. BEFORE APPLYING SECOND POUR, TOP OF FIRST POUR IS TO BE THOROUGHLY CLEANED AND A GOOD
CONCRETE COMPOUND (LATEX OR EPOXY) APPLIED.
REINFORCING:
1. REINFORCING STEEL SHALL NOT BE EXPOSED TO ELEMENTS FOR AN EXTENDED PERIOD OF TIME AND
SHALL BE STORED IN A COVERED DRY PLACE IF NECESSARY.
2. ALL REINFORCING STEEL SHALL CONFORM TO ASTM A615 GRADE 60.
3. MINIMUM CLEAR COVER OF CONCRETE OVER STEEL SHALL CONFORM TO ACI 318-08 AS FOLLOWS UNLESS
NOTED OTHERWISE IN DETAIL DRAWINGS:
CONCRETE IN PERMANENT CONTACT WITH EARTH ........ 3"
CONCRETE ABOVE GROUND ............................................... 2"
4. ALL REINFORCING SHALL BE RIGIDLY SECURED IN POSITION AND VERIFIED PRIOR TO PLACING CONCRETE.
TACK WELDING MAY BE PERFORMED ONLY WITH THE PRIOR APPROVAL OF THE ENGINEER.

GENERAL SPECIFICATIONS
1.1 SCOPE
A. PROVIDE A COMPLETE ELECTRICAL SYSTEM IN ACCORDANCE WITH ALL SPECIFICATIONS, DRAWINGS, CODES AND CONDITIONS OF THE CONTRACT.
1.2 CODES, STANDARDS, FEES, PERMITS
A. COMPLY WITH THE 2017 EDITION OF THE NATIONAL ELECTRICAL CODE, 2016 NATIONAL ELECTRICAL SAFETY CODE, ORDINANCES, AND GOVERNING CODES, WHETHER INDICATED ON THE
DRAWINGS, SPECIFIED HEREIN OR NOT.
B. SECURE ALL INSPECTIONS, FEES, PERMITS, ETC., REQUIRED BY LOCAL AND STATE AGENCIES.
1.3 DRAWINGS
A. ELECTRICAL DRAWINGS ARE DIAGRAMMATIC AND DO NOT SHOW ALL FEATURES OF THE WORK. INSTALL ELECTRICAL ITEMS TO PROVIDE SYMMETRICAL APPEARANCE. VERIFY FIELD
CONDITIONS.
1.4 WORKMANSHIP
A. CONSIDERED AS IMPORTANT AS ELECTRICAL AND MECHANICAL EFFICIENCY. COMPLETED WORK SUBJECT TO OWNER'S APPROVAL. EMPLOY WORKMEN SKILLED IN THE TRADE AND
FAMILIAR WITH THE PARTICULAR TECHNIQUES APPLICABLE TO VARIOUS SECTIONS OF WORK.
1.5 COORDINATION
A. VERIFY INFORMATION SHOWN ON DRAWINGS WITH EQUIPMENT ITEMS ACTUALLY FURNISHED.
INSTALLATION
BUS WELDING SPECIFICATIONS
2.1 ALUMINUM BUS
3.1 PREPARATION
A. ALUMINUM BUS SHALL BE EXTRUDED ALUMINUM TUBE, 6063-T6 ALUMINUM ALLOY, SCHEDULE 40, IN STANDARD PIPE SIZES. ALL DIMENSIONS REFERENCED SHALL BE IRON PIPE SIZES (IPS.)
A. A MILDLY ALKALINE SOLUTION OR A COMMERCIAL DEGREASING SOLUTION WHICH WILL NOT EVOLVE TOXIC FUMES DURING WELDING SHALL BE USED TO REMOVE SURFACE CONTAMINANTS.
B. ALUMINUM BUS SHALL BE INSTALLED AS INDICATED ON THE DRAWINGS. BUS CONNECTIONS SHALL BE COMPRESSION (EXCEPT WHERE NOTED OTHERWISE) AS INDICATED AND SHALL BE
B. ALL SURFACES SHALL BE DRIED AFTER CLEANING TO AVOID POROSITY IN THE WELD METAL.
INSTALLED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE MANUFACTURER'S INSTRUCTIONS. FOR BUS FITTINGS & CONNECTIONS DESIGNATED AS WELDED, SEE "BUS WELDING SPECIFICATIONS" SECTION ON
THIS DRAWING FOR WELDED BUS SPECIFICATIONS AND INSTALLATION INSTRUCTIONS. C. THE OXIDE FILM ON THE SURFACE SHALL BE COMPLETELY REMOVED BY WIRE BRUSHING WITH CLEAN BRUSHES OR ABRADED BY A SUITABLE ABRASIVE COMPOUND PRIOR TO JOINING THE
SURFACES.
C. BUS SPLICES SHALL BE KEPT TO A MINIMUM. PRIOR TO CUTTING THE BUS, PREPARE A BUS-CUTTING SCHEDULE OUTLINING THE NUMBER AND LENGTH OF CUT PIECES SO THAT BUS
D. THE WELD SHALL BE MADE PROMPTLY AFTER REMOVAL OF THE FILM, AND THE WELDING SURFACES SHALL BE PROTECTED FROM OXIDATION DURING THE WELDING PROCESS.
COUPLINGS WILL BE MINIMIZED.
D. AFTER CUTTING AND FITTING THE BUS, ABRADE THE END OF THE BUS WITH A STAINLESS STEEL BRUSH TO REMOVE ANY OXIDE. AFTER POLISHING, COAT THE COMPRESSION END WITH AN 3.2 ASSEMBLY
APPROVED OXIDE-INHIBITING COMPOUND.
A. ALL BUS COMPONENTS SHALL BE PROPERLY POSITIONED AS SHOWN ON THE MANUFACTURER'S DRAWING FOR EACH FITTING.
E. IN EACH HORIZONTAL BUS RUN, TEN (10) FEET IN LENGTH OR LONGER, INSTALL ONE (1) VIBRATION DAMPENING CONDUCTOR PER TABLE SHOWN ON THIS SHEET. ACSR MAY BE
SUBSTITUTED FOR AAC AS SHOWN IN THE BILL OF MATERIALS. B. POSITIONING SHALL BE CHECKED FOR RADIAL AND AXIAL ALIGNMENT WITH OTHER FITTINGS WHICH MAY BE INSTALLED ON A PARTICULAR LENGTH OF BUS.
C. THE FITTINGS SHALL BE FIXED IN THE PROPER POSITION ON THE BUS BY A MECHANICAL MEANS SUFFICIENT TO MAINTAIN ALIGNMENT DURING THE WELDING PROCESS.
F. BUS SECTIONS, FITTINGS, AND CONNECTORS SHALL BE INSTALLED AS INDICATED ON THE DRAWINGS. BENDS SHALL NOT BE FLATTENED OR KINKED. BUS ALIGNMENT SHALL NOT PUT
STRAIN ON THE INSULATORS OR EQUIPMENT OTHER THAN THE WEIGHT OF THE BUS.
3.3 PREHEAT
G. A STATIC-FREE CONNECTION SHALL BE PROVIDED ON ALL SLIP TYPE OR EXPANSION TYPE BUS SUPPORT FITTINGS.
A. IN ORDER TO MINIMIZE THE TEMPERATURE GRADIENT, AND TO BRING THE TEMPERATURE TO A POINT FOR RAPID WELDING, PREHEAT SHALL BE USED ON THE SURFACES TO BE WELDED.
H. DRILL A 3/8" WEEP HOLE IN THE BOTTOM OF ALL HORIZONTAL BUS RUNS AT THE LOW POINT OF EACH SPAN. ALL VERTICAL BUS RUNS, INCLUDING A-TAPS, SHALL BE DRILLED WITH A 3/8"
B. THE SURFACE OF ALL MEMBERS WITHIN SIX INCHES OF THE WELD SHALL BE HEATED TO A TEMPERATURE OF 400 DEGREES FAHRENHEIT PRIOR TO BEGINNING THE WELD.
WEEP HOLE AT THE LOWEST POINT IN THE BUS. IF A HORIZONTAL BUS RUN DOES NOT HAVE A LOW POINT, DRILL WEEP HOLES AT THE MIDPOINT OF THE SPAN.
I. AFTER INSTALLATION OF THE BUS, POLISH SMOOTH ALL SCRATCHES, BURRS, OR RAISED AREAS ON THE BUS TO MINIMIZE CORONA AND RADIO FREQUENCY EMISSIONS.
3.4 METHOD
2.2 EQUIPMENT MOUNTING
A. THE METHOD OF MAKING THE WELD SHALL BE ONE WHICH GIVES A CLEAN WELD AT A HIGH WELDING SPEED.
A. ALL BUS WORK, FITTINGS, INSULATORS, SWITCHES, ETC. SHALL BE ASSEMBLED AS INDICATED. ALL SWITCHES SHALL BE ADJUSTED FOR ALIGNMENT, CONTACT PRESSURE, ETC., IN B. THE GAS TUNGSTEN ARC WELDING (GTAW) OR TUNGSTEN INERT-GAS (TIG) PROCESS SHALL BE USED FOR WELDING BUS AND FITTINGS.
ACCORDANCE WITH THE MANUFACTURER'S INSTRUCTIONS. AN APPROVED OXIDE-INHIBITING COMPOUND SHALL BE APPLIED TO ALL BOLTED ALUMINUM CONNECTIONS.

DRILLED WITHIN 24 HOURS OF PLACING CONCRETE. CASING SHALL BE REQUIRED WHEN NECESSARY TO
PREVENT CAVING OF THE SOIL AND TO SEAL SURFACE WATER.
4. COLD WEATHER PROCEDURE SHALL APPLY BELOW 40 DEGREES F, PER A.C.I. 306.
5. NO CONCRETE HOTTER THAN 95 DEGREES F. SHALL BE PLACED.
6. DURING HOT WEATHER, CONCRETE SHALL BE KEPT MOIST FOR AT LEAST ONE DAY OR TREATED WITH
MEMBRANE TYPE CURING COMPOUND TO MINIMIZE SURFACE CRACKING. ADDITIONAL HOT WEATHER
PROCEDURES SHALL APPLY DURING HOT WEATHER CONCRETING PER A.C.I. 305R.
7. CHAMFER ALL EXPOSED EDGES 3/4" UNLESS NOTED OTHERWISE.
8. LEVELING NUTS SHALL BE USED ON ALL STRUCTURES SUPPORTED BY PIERS AND SECURED IN PLACE BY
ANCHOR BOLTS. DISTANCE BETWEEN THE TOP OF CONCRETE AND THE BOTTOM OF BASE PLATE SHALL
BE EQUAL TO OR LESS THAN TWO TIMES THE DIAMETER OF THE ANCHOR BOLT.
9. ALL FOUNDATION DESIGNS ARE PERFORMED IN ACCORDANCE WITH A.C.I. STANDARD 318-08.
10. SQUARE CAP DEPTH SHALL BE BELOW SUBGRADE ELEVATION AS SHOWN ON FOUNDATION DETAILS.
11. MONOLITHIC CONCRETE APPLICATIONS ARE DESIRED. BUT, IF MORE THAN ONE POUR IS NECESSARY THE
FOLLOWING PROCEDURE SHALL BE IMPLEMENTED:
A. CONCRETE IN INITIAL POUR TO BE LEFT PILED HIGH IN CENTER OF PIER.
B. AFTER FIRST HOUR, PIER HOLES SHALL BE COVERED WITH PLASTIC UNTIL READY FOR SECOND POUR.
C. BEFORE APPLYING SECOND POUR, TOP OF FIRST POUR IS TO BE THOROUGHLY CLEANED AND A GOOD
CONCRETE COMPOUND (LATEX OR EPOXY) APPLIED.
REINFORCING:
1. REINFORCING STEEL SHALL NOT BE EXPOSED TO ELEMENTS FOR AN EXTENDED PERIOD OF TIME AND
SHALL BE STORED IN A COVERED DRY PLACE IF NECESSARY.
2. ALL REINFORCING STEEL SHALL CONFORM TO ASTM A615 GRADE 60.
3. MINIMUM CLEAR COVER OF CONCRETE OVER STEEL SHALL CONFORM TO ACI 318-08 AS FOLLOWS UNLESS
NOTED OTHERWISE IN DETAIL DRAWINGS:
CONCRETE IN PERMANENT CONTACT WITH EARTH ........ 3"
CONCRETE ABOVE GROUND ............................................... 2"
4. ALL REINFORCING SHALL BE RIGIDLY SECURED IN POSITION AND VERIFIED PRIOR TO PLACING CONCRETE.
TACK WELDING MAY BE PERFORMED ONLY WITH THE PRIOR APPROVAL OF THE ENGINEER.
